+<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
+https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mr-boxington/trails/11

+
+Existing Cargo projects may already have a real `target/` from builds that ran before mbx or outside an interactive terminal. mbx can now bring those outputs under its managed-target policy without deleting them: it moves the directory under the managed root and leaves a `target` link in its place.
+
+## Adopt existing directories
+
+The new `mbx adopt` command works on one checkout or searches below one or more directories:
+
+```sh
+mbx adopt                            # current checkout
+mbx adopt ~/src/project              # one checkout
+mbx adopt --recursive ~/src          # every eligible checkout below ~/src
+mbx adopt --recursive --dry-run ~/src
+```
+
+Each result reports the target directory's logical size, and multi-checkout runs print a total. Recursive searches skip hidden directories, target directories, and symbolic links.
+
+mbx leaves a checkout unchanged and explains why when Cargo uses another target directory, the path is a workspace member rather than its root, managed targets are disabled, `target/` is already a link, or the directory is on another filesystem from the managed root. Adoption never copies or deletes a target directory.
+
+## Safe build-time adoption
+
+Interactive Cargo commands through mbx now offer to move an existing `target/`, with “Move target/” selected by default. Non-interactive commands never prompt or change the directory. When a cross-filesystem move is impossible, the prompt retains the previous removal option with “Keep it” selected by default.
+
+Before moving a directory, mbx takes Cargo's build locks and refuses if a build is still writing there. It creates the managed record and link around the rename and restores the original directory if placement fails. Once adopted, the directory follows the usual age, size, and deleted-checkout collection rules.
+
+Adoption preserves existing files, but plain Cargo and mbx key some artifacts differently. The first mbx build may therefore recompile artifacts created without mbx; a directory previously built through mbx remains fresh after adoption.
+
+## Validation
+
+- `cargo fmt --all --check`
+- `cargo test -p mbx adopt` (8 focused tests)
+- documentation build (53 pages and social metadata)
+- offline documentation link and fragment check (4,483 links, 0 errors)
